title: Attribution-Guided Shared-Private Decoupling for Noise-Reduced Audio-Visual Representation Learning
claim: Supervise decoupled shared and private representations using attribution-selected token subviews, with a lightweight truncated attribution step that scores token relevance.
layout: 2 panels, top-to-bottom flow in (a), mirrored audio/visual branches in (b)
description: The figure has two panels. Panel (a), "Training Pipeline", is a wide box. Audio tokens (green) and visual tokens (blue) enter at the top. Each stream splits into an LTA-score-sorted branch and a random-mask branch. The sorted branch yields relevant and residual token subsets (A_R, A_T, V_T, V_R), which pass through stop-gradient teacher encoders. The masked branch passes through student encoders. Small colored token squares (green, orange, blue) at the bottom represent shared and private embeddings. Red lines run from these embeddings to three red loss boxes: Audio Anchor Loss, Contrastive Loss and Visual Anchor Loss. Panel (b), "Layer-Truncated Attribution", is a purple-tinted box. It shows mirrored visual and audio branches that pass through encoders. CLS tokens are combined by a dot-product node, and attention and gradient boxes lead to yellow relevance-score token rows. Dashed blue arrows mark stop-gradient (sg). The eye goes first to the two panel titles, then to the colorful encoder boxes.
caption: Overall pipeline of our proposed framework. (a) Attribution-guided teacher-student training. A pretrained teacher generates high-relevance shared-cover subviews and low-relevance residual complements, which serve as stop-gradient anchors for training the student's shared and private tokens. For clarity, we omit the MAE branch inherited from the baseline [ref]. (b) Layer-Truncated Attribution (LTA). Given the cross-modal matching score, LTA computes CLS-to-token gradient-attention relevance from the last Transformer block.
abstract: Audio-visual representation learning commonly aligns paired audio and visual signals with sample-level contrastive objectives. However, real-world audio-visual pairs usually contain heterogeneous patch tokens: only a subset carries reliable cross-modal shared semantics, while many others mainly encode modality-private residuals. Aggregating all tokens into a single global representation can therefore introduce semantic noise into cross-modal alignment. Motivated by the minimal-sufficiency principle, we propose an attribution-guided shared-private decoupling framework to mitigate this issue. Our key idea is to identify shared-cover subviews that preserve dominant cross-modal information while suppressing modality-private residuals, and use them to supervise decoupled shared and private representations. To identify such subviews efficiently, we draw on transformer attribution method and introduce Layer-Truncated Attribution (LTA), which provides a lightweight estimate of token-level relevance to cross-modal shared information. We further adopt a teacher-student framework, where the teacher provides attribution-induced supervision and the student internalizes shared-private decoupling into its representations, without introducing extra inference cost. Experiments on retrieval, classification, and sound-prompted semantic segmentation show consistent gains over strong baselines. Compared with baseline, our method improves the average zero-shot R@1 by 4.0 across AudioSet and VGGSound retrieval, and improves AS20K classification mAP by 3.1, demonstrating the effectiveness of fine grained attribution guidance for reducing semantic noise.reducing semantic noise. Code will be released at https://github.com/wanglg20/LTA
